increments.title: Animals: page maturity moves into feature folders
increments.brief: Move each page's maturity level out of src/server/app/page-maturity/page-levels.js and into its feature folder: the feature's page.js gains `maturity` (one of LEVELS in page-maturity/levels.js). A page with no level set is exploring. The banner (page-maturity.js) finds the level from the matched route's page, not from route patterns, so PAGE_LEVELS, SECTION_LEVELS and isInSection go, and page-levels.js and its test are deleted. Pages outside the journey feature folders (the start page, dashboards) still need a home: give them the nearest equivalent (their own route module or feature folder) rather than keeping a pattern table. Keep today's levels exactly: the start page exploring, every notification journey page detailing. Keep the banner switch, copy, tags and error-page rule unchanged. Unit tests prove a page's level comes from its folder and the default is exploring; update docs that describe page-levels.js.

increments.title: Plants: page maturity moves into feature folders
increments.brief: Same change as F1 (already landed in trade-imports-animals-frontend on this branch: read its commit with `git -C <animals> log -1 -p` and follow it) for trade-imports-plants-frontend. Keep today's levels exactly: every page exploring.

increments.title: INS: page maturity moves into feature folders
increments.brief: Same change as F1 for trade-imports-ins-frontend. Its features/ folders have no page.js, so pick the closest equivalent the repo already uses for per-feature metadata (or add a small `maturity` export beside the feature's routes) and say which in notes. Keep today's levels exactly: every page exploring.

increments.title: Frontends: a Signed-off pages pull request check
increments.brief: Canary on animals, then plants and INS. Add a script (with unit tests) that, given a base ref, lists changed test files (*.test.js, *.fit.spec.js, snapshots) inside feature folders whose maturity is agreed or readyForLive, plus deletions of such files. Add it as a job in .github/workflows/check-pull-request.yml that writes a plain-English summary (page, files, 'a signed-off page's tests changed: this needs a person's decision, see the linked Jira ticket') to the job summary and fails the job when anything is listed. It is not a required check, so it flags rather than blocks. It must not need the workspace repo. Today no page is signed off, so it passes on every pull request: prove it trips with a unit test using a fixture folder at agreed. Same script and job in all three repos.

increments.title: openspec: a Maturity line on page specs and a Signed off mark on scenarios
increments.brief: Add two conventions to openspec/config.yaml (and docs/reference/openspec.md): a `**Maturity**: <exploring|detailing|agreed|readyForLive>` line under each journey-pages page spec's Purpose, and a `**Signed off**: <YYYY-MM-DD>` line on a scenario (after its ID line), allowed in any spec, which marks it as part of a signed-off page's contract. Extend tim spec lint (tim/src/spec/checks, with tests) so: every journey-pages spec has a valid Maturity line; a Signed off mark is well formed. Then add the Maturity line to every existing journey-pages spec across domains, using today's banner levels (animals journey pages detailing; plants and ins exploring; admin has no banner, so skip admin and make lint not require it there). No scenario is marked signed off. `tim spec lint` must be clean afterwards for every prefix it was clean for before.

increments.title: tim spec diff --signed-off
increments.brief: Extend `tim spec diff` (tim/src/spec/diff.js, tim/src/commands/spec/diff.js) with `--signed-off`. With it, the result reports only signed-off scenarios: those added, changed or removed in the commits or range given, including a Signed off mark being removed. Add `--repo <name> --base <ref>`: read that repo's changed files (under repos/<name>, against <ref>, committed and uncommitted) and report every test file linked in openspec/coverage/**/coverage.json to a signed-off scenario that was edited or deleted, naming the scenario. Output `result.signedOff` with each scenario, its capability, what happened and why it counts, and `result.ticketDraft`: plain English for a Jira ticket saying which signed-off behaviour changes, from what to what (scenario steps before and after), for people to approve or refuse. Exit 0 with nothing found; exit 3 (documented) when anything is found, so a caller can tell. --help text, README, nock-free tests with fixture specs and coverage.

increments.title: Workspace CI: spec lint and the signed-off check on openspec changes
increments.brief: Add a GitHub Actions workflow (or a job in tim-ci.yml if that fits better) that on pull requests touching openspec/ runs `tim spec lint` and `tim spec diff --signed-off` over the pull request's commits, writes the result to the job summary, and fails on lint findings or on a signed-off change. It is not a required check. Follow docs/best-practices/github-actions.md.

increments.title: Rules and the draft-plus-ticket flow
increments.brief: Write .claude/rules/signed-off-pages.md: what a signed-off page is (maturity agreed or readyForLive in its feature folder, its scenarios marked Signed off in openspec); that a change to a signed-off scenario or to a test linked to one is raised, not decided by an agent; the flow: carry on with the work, raise a Jira ticket from `tim spec diff --signed-off`'s ticketDraft via `tim jira create` (dry run, then confirm), keep every pull request on the branch as a draft with the ticket linked, and a person un-drafts or refuses; promotion of a page (check scenarios are thorough with tim spec gaps, set maturity, mark scenarios, one reviewed PR). In CLAUDE.md, add the exception to rule 6: for a test linked to a signed-off scenario, fix the code, not the test, unless a person has ruled. Keep CLAUDE.md edits small. Plain English, house style.

increments.title: Skills: spec sync in ticket, and the signed-off check before every pull request
increments.brief: The ticket skill (.claude/skills/ticket) gets a spec-sync step modelled on frontend-change's Step 5 (update openspec spec.md and coverage.json for behaviour the ticket changed, validate, tim spec lint), and both ticket and frontend-change run `tim spec diff --signed-off` (workspace range and each changed repo with --repo/--base) before raising a pull request, following .claude/rules/signed-off-pages.md on a trip. govuk-upgrade, npm-upgrade and code-style run the same check before their pull request: a trip means 'no behaviour change' work changed signed-off behaviour, so stop and raise it. review adds a finding when a diff touches a signed-off scenario or linked test with no linked ticket. Edit each SKILL.md minimally, in its own style.

increments.title: Build loop: a signed-off check after each row's spec sync
increments.brief: In .claude/skills/requirements-pipeline/workflow/increment-build-loop.js, add a stage after a row's spec sync is verified (the ladder's spec lint) and before it lands: run `tim spec diff --signed-off` on the workspace's uncommitted openspec/ change and with --repo/--base for each branched repo. On a trip: raise the Jira ticket from ticketDraft (the loop already creates tickets; reuse that path), record it on the row, leave every pull request as a draft (the loop already never un-drafts), and park the row as awaiting a signed-off ruling, with the loop carrying on with other rows that do not depend on it. With nothing found, behaviour is unchanged. Update references/BUILD.md, the backlog schema's status values if a new one is needed, and any tests that cover the loop. Keep the change small and in the file's existing patterns; this file is large, so read around each insertion point carefully.

increments.title: Lint: frontend maturity and spec Maturity lines agree
increments.brief: Extend tim spec lint (with tests) so that, when repos/ holds the frontends, each journey-pages spec's Maturity line matches the maturity in that page's feature folder (from F1-F3), and a scenario is marked Signed off only if its page is agreed or readyForLive. Map spec prefix to frontend repo with the existing prefix mapping in tim. Skip quietly when a frontend is not cloned. Must be clean on this branch.

increments.title: Canary proof on the animals frontend
increments.brief: Prove the whole flow without committing any stand-in. Temporarily: set the animals declaration page to agreed, mark its declaration spec scenarios Signed off. Then try, one at a time, reverting between: (a) edit the declaration FIT spec linked in coverage; (b) change a declaration scenario's steps; (c) a test-only change to a different, non-signed-off page; (d) a package.json devDependency version bump. For each, run tim spec lint, tim spec diff --signed-off (workspace and --repo trade-imports-animals-frontend --base origin/main) and the frontend's signed-off check script, and record what each said. Expected: (a) and (b) trip with a sensible ticketDraft, (c) and (d) pass. Write the evidence to workareas/shared/signed-off-pages/canary.md. Restore every file afterwards: both repos must show no changes except canary.md. If a result is wrong, fix the tool (with a test), commit that fix, and rerun.
